notes: §1985:XV.3.2.4 GR16: "If the first execution of the first nondeclarative procedure in the program causes the debugging section to be executed", DEBUG-LINE is that procedure's first statement, DEBUG-NAME its name and DEBUG-CONTENTS 'START PROGRAM'; anything no rule sets stays spaces (§1985:XV.3.2.4 GR11). Since PB5415 landed, EmitDispatcher emits EmitDebugCause(StartProgram) only on an instance's first activation (the __dbgStarted flag), EmitDebugRunner uses the subject's line for that cause, and DebugItem.ContentsFor writes START PROGRAM. Probed at 85 (classes b, c, d): paragraph subject F1 in a CALLed program: first CALL DS [33][F1][START PROGRAM] (line 33 = F1's first statement), second CALL DS [ ][F1][ ] (spaces), CALL after CANCEL START PROGRAM again (docs/conformance/3/D-DEBUG-PROCEDURE); a section subject S1 first: [23][S1][START PROGRAM] once though a loop GO TO F1 re-enters; ALL PROCEDURES: S0 and P0 both START PROGRAM; subject not first: F2 gets FALL THROUGH, no START PROGRAM; no DEBUGGING MODE: section not run; --std 2002: COBOL0902. Classes a, e, f do not reach a procedure trigger. The witness matches. || REFUTED: PARTIAL (harm: rejects legal source, backend crash): a USE FOR DEBUGGING ON section-name whose section has no paragraphs produces generated C# that references an undeclared __dbgItem (CS0103); the empty section is never recorded as a debug subject (ProcedureTableBuilder.AddDebugSectionSubject / FinalizeDebug have no pc for it), yet the declarative's DEBUG-ITEM references are emitted.
